newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Increase in mergers seen in Manila banking sector.
newsitem.headline: Increase in mergers seen in Manila banking sector.

text.p: The Philippine banking industry could be headed for a period of intense mergers and acquisitions following a hefty increase in the banks' minimum capital base, analysts said on Friday.

The Central Bank announced on Thursday it would require universal banks, also known as expanded commercial banks, to raise their minimum capital to 4.5 billion pesos ($171.3 million) from the present 2.5 billion pesos ($95.2 million). Commercial banks must raise theirs to 2 billion pesos from the present 1.25 billion pesos.
Existing banks have two years to comply with the new minimum capital level while new banks will have to comply immediately.

"It will initiate more consolidation in the industry. There is need for consolidation ... there's too much competition in the industry," Matthew Sutherland, research director at Philippine Asia Equity Securities, said.
In the same announcement, the Central Bank said it was cutting reserve requirements to 13 percent from 15 percent.

The Central Bank's decision on higher minimum capital requirements coincided with the announcement that AsianBank Corp, a unit of A. Soriano Corp and Phinma Group, planned to merge with PDCP Bank, an affiliate of Metro Pacific Corp
AsianBank is a leader in investment banking, while PDCP Bank is strong in consumer and retail banking. The merger, if it goes through, will go into effect in the first quarter of 1997.
AsianBank chairman Ramon del Rosario Jr said in a statement that the merger is necessary for the bank to remain competitive with large universal banks.

"There's a likelihood that many small banks will be acquired by big banks ... The (AsianBank-PDCP) merger is a sign of things to come," Audi Pantillano, banking analyst of Angping Securities, told Reuters.
He said many banks were on the lookout for possible partners in order to stay competitive in an industry that is being opened up.
Earlier this year, Bank of the Philippine Islands merged with CityTrust Banking Corp while PDCP Bank acquired the assets of First Bank of the Philippines.
Other banks which are currently seeking partners are Security Bank, Equitable Banking Corp and Union Bank of the Philippines, which is the product of a merger itself, industry sources said.
"Size is important in a liberalised environment. Banks need a lot of resources to be able to face competition," said Raul Ruiz, vice president for research at Sun Hung Kai Securities.
There are 21 universal banks and 30 commercial banks operating in the Philippines. Among them are 14 foreign banks which include branches of some of the largest banks in the world.
Johnny Noe Ravalo, economist of the Bankers Association of the Philippines, said mergers and acquisitions were one option banks could choose to comply with the new capital requirements.
"For some banks, merger might be the answer. Some banks might look for other partners, while some banks might ask current partners to produce more money. Each bank has its own strategy," Ravalo said.
